key_insight: A spectral neural constitutive model learns flexible yield surfaces and evolution laws while enforcing isotropy, convexity, and thermodynamic consistency by construction.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables learned elastoplastic material laws, including non-associative flow, to be used in finite element boundary-value simulations.
method: Use permutation-invariant eigenvalue representations to enforce isotropy and convexity across learnable components.
Represent non-associative yielding through a jointly learned additive extension of a convex flow potential.
Train through a backward-Euler return map using implicit-function gradients and eigenvalue-degeneracy-aware differentiation.
evidence_signal: Evaluation includes reproducing known constitutive models, learning from full-field finite element stress–strain data and homogenized foam responses, and solving plane-stress boundary-value problems.
watch_item: Implementation requires careful differentiation near repeated eigenvalues and robust implicit return-map solves; the stated scope is rate-independent, isotropic elastoplasticity.
paper_title: Thermodynamically consistent neural constitutive models for elastoplasticity via eigen-representations
